newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Dec 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Dec 17.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Dec. 17:

WASHINGTON - Mayor Marion Barry proposed that the District government slash $96.5 million in spending by eliminating 1,000 positions, cutting $7.9 million from the D.C. public school budget, tightening spending at the University of the District of Columbia and scaling back proposed pay raises for city managers.
WASHINGTON - President Clinton criticized Israel for creating an obstacle to peace with its new campaign to encourage Jewish settlement on the West Bank.

WASHINGTON - Researchers said they have designed a supercomputer that can handle a staggering one trillion mathematical operations per second, a breakthrough computer experts likened to the running of the first four-minute mile.

WASHINGTON - President Clinton's legal defense fund announced that it has returned $640,000 in unsolicited contributions delivered by Little Rock businessman Charles Trie because of suspicions about the source of some of the money.
ATLANTA - The legend of the Black Panther Party, the militant black group founded in the 1960s, continues to inspire.
WASHINGTON - More than 60 homosexuals claiming persecution have been granted asylum in the United States since 1994 when such claims were ruled grounds for approval.
